blocks.content: This topic ties describe, logs, exec, and Events together into an actual, systematic debugging workflow, not just four separate tools used at random.
1. A Systematic Order, Not a Random Search
blocks.text: 1. A Systematic Order, Not a Random Search

blocks.content: Rather than reaching for tools arbitrarily, a systematic order gets you to the answer fastest: describe first, then logs, then exec if the Pod is still running and more investigation is genuinely needed.

blocks.alt: A deliberate order, each step building on what the previous one revealed

blocks.content: 2. Step One: describe, for the Big Picture
blocks.text: 2. Step One: describe, for the Big Picture

blocks.content: Starting with kubectl describe, covered in its own topic, gives you the object's current status and, critically, its recent Events, this alone often reveals the actual problem before you have even looked at a single log line.

blocks.alt: The big picture and recent Events, often enough on its own to spot the issue

blocks.content: 3. Step Two: logs, for What the App Actually Said
blocks.text: 3. Step Two: logs, for What the App Actually Said

blocks.content: If describe does not fully explain things, kubectl logs, covered in its own topic, shows what the application itself printed, its own error messages, stack traces, or diagnostic output.

blocks.alt: The application's own account of what happened, in its own words

blocks.content: 4. Step Three: exec, if Still Running
blocks.text: 4. Step Three: exec, if Still Running

blocks.content: If the Pod is still alive and more investigation is genuinely needed, kubectl exec, covered in its own topic, lets you get inside directly, check a config file, test connectivity, or run a diagnostic command live.

blocks.alt: Direct, live investigation, when the first two steps were not enough on their own

blocks.content: A Pod stuck in CrashLoopBackOff: describe shows repeated restarts in its Events, logs --previous reveals the actual error the application threw right before crashing, and, if a fix requires more digging, exec into a related, still-running Pod to check shared configuration, exactly this workflow, applied to a real, common scenario.

blocks.alt: The exact workflow, applied to a real, genuinely common scenario

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A systematic debugging order, describe, then logs, then exec if still needed, gets you to the actual answer faster than reaching for tools at random.
Each step builds on the last: describe gives the big picture and Events, logs gives the application's own account, exec gives direct, live access when more is genuinely needed.
